partners.diseaseBName: STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy
partners.mechanism_chain: RBM10 (HGNC:10362) —DISRUPTS→ mRNA splicing (GO:0000375); mRNA splicing (GO:0000375) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart malformation (HP:0001627); STING1 (HGNC:17746) —INCREASES→ cGAS-STING innate immune signaling pathway (GO:0031234); cGAS-STING innate immune signaling pathway (GO:0031234) —LEADS_TO→ Vasculitis (HP:0001989); cGAS-STING innate immune signaling pathway (GO:0031234) —LEADS_TO→ Interferon signature (HP:0030179). While RBM10 (TARP syndrome) affects mRNA splicing, leading to congenital heart defects, STING1 (SAVI) mutations lead to aberrant activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, resulting in vasculitis and interferon signatures. The shared element is the STING1 gene, but the functional consequences and downstream pathways diverge significantly, making a direct mechanistic link through shared entities challenging beyond the gene itself.

While RBM10 (TARP syndrome) affects mRNA splicing, leading to congenital heart defects, STING1 (SAVI) mutations lead to aberrant activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, resulting in vasculitis and interferon signatures. The shared element is the STING1 gene, but the functional consequences and downstream pathways diverge significantly, making a direct mechanistic link through shared entities challenging beyond the gene itself.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct roles of RBM10 and STING1 in their respective disease pathways could lead to targeted therapies for each condition.
